---
title: "Execution Context"
summary: Environment variables and execution information available to code cells
---

## Overview

When Quarto runs the code cells of a document, it tells that code where it is running and how the document is being rendered. It does this through environment variables, which every language can read. One of them, `QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO`, points to a JSON file with the document's resolved format, including its brand.

Use this information to:

- find files relative to the document or the project;
- skip work that only makes sense for one output format;
- style plots and tables with the colors and fonts of your brand, in light and dark mode.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Value |
|----------|-------|
| `QUARTO_PROJECT_ROOT` | The project directory. For a document outside a project, the document's directory. |
| `QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH` | The directory of the document being rendered. |
| `QUARTO_DOCUMENT_FILE` | The file name of the document being rendered. |
| `QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO` | The path of a JSON file with [execution information](#execution-information). |
| `QUARTO_FIG_WIDTH` | Default figure width in inches (`fig-width`). |
| `QUARTO_FIG_HEIGHT` | Default figure height in inches (`fig-height`). |
| `QUARTO_FIG_DPI` | Default figure resolution (`fig-dpi`). |
| `QUARTO_FIG_FORMAT` | Default figure format (`fig-format`). For `retina`, Quarto reports `png` at twice the resolution. |
| `QUARTO_PROFILE` | The active [project profiles](../projects/profiles.qmd), comma-separated. |

::: panel-tabset
## Python

``` python
import os
print(os.environ["QUARTO_DOCUMENT_FILE"])
```

## R

``` r
Sys.getenv("QUARTO_DOCUMENT_FILE")
```

## Julia

``` julia
ENV["QUARTO_DOCUMENT_FILE"]
```
:::

## Execution information

`QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO` holds the path of a JSON file. The file exists while the document's code runs; read it from a cell, not after the render.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `document-path` | The absolute path of the document. |
| `format` | The resolved format, in six parts (below). |

The `format` object has these parts:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `identifier` | `target-format` (as written, such as `html` or `acm-html`), `base-format` (such as `html`), and `display-name` (such as `HTML`). |
| `execute` | Execution options: `eval`, `echo`, `output`, `warning`, `error`, `include`, `fig-width`, `fig-height`, `fig-dpi`, `fig-format`, and any other `execute` option the document sets. |
| `render` | Rendering options, such as `code-fold` and `keep-tex`, and the document's [brand](#brand). |
| `pandoc` | Pandoc options, such as `to` and `toc`. |
| `language` | The localized text Quarto uses for this document, such as `callout-tip-title`. |
| `metadata` | Everything else in the document's metadata, such as `title`, including project-level settings. |

::: panel-tabset
## Python

``` python
import json, os

with open(os.environ["QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO"]) as f:
    info = json.load(f)

print(info["format"]["identifier"]["base-format"])
```

## R

``` r
info <- jsonlite::fromJSON(Sys.getenv("QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO"))
info$format$identifier$`base-format`
```

## Julia

``` julia
using JSON
info = JSON.parsefile(ENV["QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO"])
info["format"]["identifier"]["base-format"]
```
:::

### Running code only for some formats

Conditional content (`.content-visible`, `.content-hidden`) controls whether output is *shown*; the code inside still runs. To skip the work itself, read the format in the cell:

``` python
import json, os

with open(os.environ["QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO"]) as f:
    info = json.load(f)

if info["format"]["identifier"]["base-format"] in ("html", "dashboard", "revealjs"):
    # interactive output only for HTML-based formats
    ...
```

### Brand

When the document has a [brand](brand.qmd), `format.render.brand` holds it once per color mode:

- `light` is always present;
- `dark` is present when the brand defines dark values: a color with a `dark:` value, or a separate dark brand file (`brand: {light: ..., dark: ...}`).

Each mode has `data`, the brand as written in `_brand.yml` with the colors for that mode, and `brandDir`, the directory the brand file is in.

``` python
import json, os

with open(os.environ["QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO"]) as f:
    brand = json.load(f)["format"]["render"].get("brand", {})

for mode, entry in brand.items():
    colors = entry["data"].get("color", {})
    print(mode, colors.get("background"), colors.get("foreground"))
```

## Engines

The knitr engine and Jupyter kernels for Python, R and Julia see all of these variables.

Quarto sets the values inside the document's Jupyter kernel before the document's first cell runs, on every render, so a kernel that `q2 preview` keeps running between re-renders still sees current values. For kernels in other languages, Quarto cannot set them.

The `julia` and `marimo` engines do not receive these variables yet.

## Migrating from Quarto 1

The variable names and the JSON layout are the same as in Quarto 1. The differences:

- A `_brand.yml` file is used only when a `brand:` key names it, so `format.render.brand` is absent without one. See [Brand](brand.qmd).
- `format.render.brand.dark` is present whenever the brand defines dark values. Quarto 1 also includes it when the document turns dark mode on for a brand without dark values; that dark entry repeated the light one.
- Each brand mode has `data` and `brandDir`. Quarto 1 also includes other internal fields, such as `processedData`.
- `QUARTO_FIG_*` report the figure options Quarto 2 uses. For HTML, Quarto 1 defaults to `retina` and reports `png` at 192 dpi; Quarto 2 reports `png` at 96 dpi.
- The `execute` part lists the default visibility and figure options. Quarto 1 also includes other per-format defaults.
